sources.title: Carbon footprint for the UK and England to 2023
Provisional road traffic year ending March 2026

packages.title: Defra carbon-footprint consumption-basis QA
facts: Updated 24 July 2026; measures GHG associated with UK consumption.
2023 UK carbon footprint estimated at 699 MtCO2e, 4% below 2022.
2023 remained below the 2007 peak of 984 MtCO2e.
Consumption-basis totals are not parcel emissions.

packages.title: Defra carbon-footprint import correction QA
facts: The page records a 7 July 2026 correction to EU-import narrative text.
The corrected wording distinguishes imported-emissions share from total UK footprint share.
Correction history must remain attached to reused values.
Import-related footprint emissions are not territorial or parcel values.

packages.title: Defra carbon-footprint revision-history QA
facts: The collection records annual updates and prior corrections.
A 30 June 2026 annual update and 7 July correction are both recorded.
Earlier table and multiplier corrections show edition provenance matters.
Revised national models must not be silently converted to parcel values.

packages.title: ONS three-basis comparability QA
facts: ONS distinguishes territorial, residence and footprint GHG measures.
Territorial 2025 emissions were estimated at 367 MtCO2e.
Residence-basis 2024 emissions were provisionally estimated at 478 MtCO2e.
Different bases and reference years are not interchangeable or parcel-specific.

packages.title: ONS residence industry/household scope QA
facts: Residence-basis 2024 emissions were 478 MtCO2e.
Households were the largest single contributor at 25.9%.
Industries collectively accounted for 74.1%.
Economic-sector shares are not cadastral parcel boundaries.

packages.title: ONS direct-energy mix and intensity QA
facts: 2024 GHG intensity was about 140 tCO2e per £1 million GVA.
Intensity was 72% lower than in 1990.
Fossil fuels were 77.7% and renewables 15.3% of direct energy consumption.
Energy mix/intensity context is not direct parcel measurement.

packages.title: ONS atmospheric current/provisional scope QA
facts: Dataset covers CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs, SF6 and NF3 plus total GHG.
Current edition provides all economic sectors; provisional provides top-level estimates.
Coverage is around 130 SIC categories for 1990 to 2024.
Current/provisional editions must not be mixed without labels.

packages.title: ONS atmospheric correction-history QA
facts: ONS separates scheduled revisions from genuine corrections.
A 2 March 2026 correction fixed incorrect 2023 CO2 values for specified industries.
Superseded editions remain available for provenance.
Correction history does not create parcel-level evidence.

packages.title: ONS quarterly temporal-disaggregation QA
facts: ONS quarterly residence-basis GHG estimates use Chow-Lin temporal disaggregation.
Latest listed edition covers Q3 2025.
These are modelled quarterly estimates, not direct quarterly inventories.
Quarterly residence estimates are not parcel measurements.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 provisional territorial-total QA
facts: Published 2 April 2026; 2025 territorial GHG provisionally 367 MtCO2e.
Total was 2% below 2024 and 54% below 1990.
Final 2025 estimates are due in February 2027.
National territorial totals do not provide parcel values.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 provisional sector-share QA
facts: Domestic transport 31%, buildings/product uses 22%, agriculture 13%.
Industry 11%, electricity supply 10%, fuel supply 7%, waste 6%.
LULUCF was about 0.1% of net emissions.
National source-sector shares are not parcel observations.

packages.title: DESNZ domestic-transport boundary QA
facts: Domestic transport includes roads, domestic aviation/shipping, fishing and rail.
It excludes international aviation/shipping from the territorial total.
CO2 represented 98% of domestic-transport emissions in 2025.
Sector totals require local activity/spatial evidence before parcel use.

packages.title: DESNZ buildings/product-use boundary QA
facts: Sector includes building fuel combustion and multiple product-use emissions.
Residential combustion is the largest component; commercial/public buildings are separate components.
Industrial buildings are reported under industry instead.
Building-sector totals do not identify cadastral parcels.

packages.title: DESNZ international bunker memo-item QA
facts: International aviation/shipping bunker emissions are reported separately as memo items.
They are excluded from the UK territorial total under UNFCCC reporting.
2025 aviation bunkers fell about 1%; shipping bunkers fell about 6% versus 2024.
UK-port/airport bunkering does not automatically equal adjacent-parcel emissions.

packages.title: DESNZ provisional held-constant methodology QA
facts: Provisional GHG estimates rely heavily on provisional energy statistics.
Some components without timely data are held constant from 2024.
Some non-energy components use projections.
Provisional modelling is not a direct parcel measurement.

packages.title: DESNZ Energy Trends activity-context QA
facts: 30 June 2026 release provides provisional monthly production, trade, generation and consumption.
Statistics are split by coal, oil, gas and electricity.
These are energy-activity statistics rather than GHG measurements.
Emissions conversion requires compatible factors, periods and local activity.

packages.title: DESNZ local-GHG point-source context QA
facts: Local/regional release supports local-authority and sector filtering.
It identifies significant point sources such as iron and steel plants.
Local-authority totals are broader than any individual parcel.
Point-source candidates still require facility-to-parcel identity and geometry.

packages.title: DESNZ local-GHG uncertainty/method QA
facts: Technical report documents electricity, gas, industrial, agriculture, domestic, transport, LULUCF and waste methods.
It includes an uncertainty-analysis section.
Different source categories use different allocation methods.
Local-authority estimates alone must not be treated as parcel emissions.

packages.title: DfT 2025 road-traffic activity QA
facts: 2025 GB motor traffic estimated at 342.6 billion vehicle miles.
Cars 262.4, vans 58.8 and lorries 16.3 billion vehicle miles.
Overall traffic was 1.9% above 2024.
Traffic activity requires vehicle/fuel factors before emissions use.

packages.title: DfT road-link quality-boundary QA
facts: Annual estimates use about 7,000 manual roadside counts plus automatic counters and road lengths.
National/regional estimates are robust; individual links/small areas are less robust.
Counted link records are generally more accurate than Estimated records.
Road-link traffic is activity, not parcel GHG measurement.

packages.title: DfT provisional YE-March-2026 versus annual-2025 QA
facts: Year ending March 2026 provisional motor traffic was 343.2 billion vehicle miles.
Cars 262.7, vans 59.2 and lorries 16.3 billion vehicle miles.
Motorways 72.0, A roads 152.0, minor roads 119.2 billion vehicle miles.
Year-ending-March provisional data must not be mixed with calendar-year final data.

packages.title: DfT Q1-2026 port-freight provisional QA
facts: Q1 2026 major-port statistics are provisional.
Total freight 104.7 Mt; inward 72.3 Mt; outward 32.5 Mt.
Unitised traffic was 4.7 million units; rolling-year tonnage 416.7 Mt.
Freight activity is not port-parcel GHG measurement.

packages.title: DfT port-freight revision/period guard QA
facts: Quarterly port statistics are provisional before annual finalisation.
Historical port data can be revised after provider engagement.
London 2019-2023 and some Hull 2019 data were revised in the 2024 publication.
Revision and period status must stay attached to activity evidence.

packages.title: Environment Agency PI media/scope QA
facts: Pollution Inventory covers annual mass releases to air, controlled waters and sewers.
It also records waste transferred off site.
Reporting covers the whole authorisation/permit and can include point and fugitive releases.
Permit totals and waste transfers are not automatically parcel air-emissions values.

packages.title: EA IED permit decision versus emissions QA
facts: EA publishes dated 2026 IED permit decisions, variations, notices and surrenders.
A permit decision demonstrates regulatory status, not a measured GHG amount.
Permit identifiers and decision dates must be preserved separately from emissions years.
Postal location/permit issuance alone cannot establish parcel emissions.

packages.title: EA landfill residual-methane measurement QA
facts: EA research evaluated methods for measuring landfill methane.
Residual methane can arise from multiple sources across a wide site, making measurement difficult.
Landfill-gas collection is mandatory for permitted biodegradable-waste landfills in England.
Parcel methane needs site-specific measurement/model evidence plus geometry.

packages.title: EA landfill MCE normal-operation QA
facts: Survey-derived methane collection efficiency can indicate changes in gas management.
Measurements should be taken under normal operating conditions.
Normal conditions should be supported by long- and short-term gas-collection data.
Site-performance metrics still require verified parcel geometry before parcel use.

packages.title: UK ETS registry emissions/surrenders QA
facts: Registry publishes installation and aircraft account/allocation reports.
2026 installation allocation reports were published 5 July 2026.
Compliance report published 22 June 2026 covers emissions and surrendered allowances for 2021-2025.
Allocation/surrender records are not automatically verified parcel-emissions totals.
